title: Linux Permissions: Who Can Do What?

scenes.say: Who can read this file? And how do you check? Let's break down Linux permissions.
Every file has three sets of permissions: owner, group, and others.
Read, write, and execute map to numbers: read is four, write is two, execute is one. Add them up for each role.

scenes.title: ls -l config.yml
scenes.say: Use ls dash l to see permissions. Here, only root can read or write config dot y m l.

scenes.label: Defaults
scenes.say: Remember: use seven fifty five for scripts, six forty four for files, and six hundred for private keys.

scenes.question: App can't read config. What next?
scenes.right: Check ownership and set mode to 640.
scenes.say: Interview trap: If your app can't read its config, don't just set permissions wide open. Check the owner and set the mode to six forty.
